liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Jack Straw** (2 reviews): Attendee calls this specific performance the best Jack Straw they have ever seen or heard; Listener describes this as one of the longest and most badass versions of the song [23][27]
- **Shakedown Street** (1 review): Second set opener featured Jerry ripping huge wah solos, described as very funky and classic [29]

## The recordings

- **gd1984-10-20.aud.morris.108407.flac24** (recommended): audience recording; 21 songs; 156 min [1]
- **gd1984-10-20.nak300.carpenter.wise.andrewf.33341.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 21 songs; 152 min; rated 4.25/5 by 4 [5]. Said about its sound: Recording is described as really hot and seriously in your face, with brief left channel muffling [5]
- **gd1984-10-20.154034.mtx.photoleon.flac1644**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 158 min; rated 1/5 by 1 [11]
- **gd1984-10-20.150967.sbd.eaton-latvala.miller.flac1644**: soundboard; 19 songs; 163 min [12]
- **gd84-10-20.sbd.mattman.15673.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 152 min; rated 4.05/5 by 42 [15]. Said about its sound: Review emphasizes hearing the full song composite, including drums and piano, not just licks; Review notes Healy manipulated Garcia's voice with delay, and reverb was clear from the balcony [22][26]

## Around the show

- Weir told the crowd to step back with weary resignation, leading to an angry performance [24]
- SU student noted front crowd refused to move back, initially making the show a buzzkill [25]
- Bobby sounded tired and aggravated pleading with the crowd, while Jerry appeared deeply out of it [28]
- Reviewer flew from Florida to Syracuse specifically to see this show after hearing about new material [30]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1984-10-20.aud.morris.108407.flac24**: taped by Bob Morris; source: Nakamichi CM-300 (CP-1) x2 > Cassette Master (Sony TCD5M/Maxell XLII-S C-90) Cassette Master (Nakamichi DR-1) > Korg MR-1000 (1-bit/5.6MHz) > Audiogate… [1]
- **gd1984-10-20.nak300.carpenter.wise.andrewf.33341.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Ted Carpenter; transferred by Jim Wise and Andrew F.; source: FOB, Nakamichi CM-300's with CP-4 shotgun capsules > Sony TC-D5M > MAC (UD-XLII, no Dolby) [5]
- **gd1984-10-20.154034.mtx.photoleon.flac1644**: source: Matrix created in Adobe Audition by Joe Noel June 2021 [11]. Also: Source lineage includes a master cassette shared by Anon and an SBD recording by Rob Eaton [11]
- **gd1984-10-20.150967.sbd.eaton-latvala.miller.flac1644**: transferred by Original Transfer and Mastering by Rob Eaton Additional Mastering by Charlie Miller  November 28, 2020; source: SBD > PCM Master > DAT (Panasonic SV-3700) > DAT (Panasonic SV-3800) [12]. Also: Source is an SBD recording provided by Rob Eaton and Dick Latvala, with small patches [12]
- **gd84-10-20.sbd.mattman.15673.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD> CM> DAT> computer processing> CDR> EAC> SHNTOOL> MKWACT [15]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Steve Schneider Grateful Dead: [1984-10-20 Carrier Dome, Syracuse U., Syracuse, NY, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1984-10-20-carrier-dome-syracuse-u-syracuse-ny-usa/) [35]
- Fan art by Tim O'Shea: [Grateful Dead Take One Last Step Back in the Carrier Dome: 10/20/84](https://nysmusic.com/2024/10/19/grateful-dead-take-one-last-step-back-in-the-carrier-dome-10-20-84/) [36]
- Poster by Steve Schneider Grateful Dead: [1984-10-20 Carrier Dome, Syracuse U., Syracuse, NY, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1984-10-20-carrier-dome-syracuse-u-syracuse-ny-usa/) [37]
- Poster by Pete Mason: [Revisit the Grateful Dead at the Carrier Dome – October 20, 1984](https://nysmusic.com/2020/05/24/revisit-the-grateful-dead-at-the-carrier-dome-in-october-1984/) [38]
